en: Please enjoy my conversation with Neil Mova.

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe just orient us there with a brief description, like literally what the system is that you're building and why it should exist.

speaker: Unknown
en: CLResearch is a token factory.
zh: CLResearch 是一个代币工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an API where anyone can send us requests where they can use large language models, open source language models for any test they want.

speaker: Unknown
en: We will serve those tokens to them at a price that is unbeatable in the market.
zh: 我们以市场上无可匹敌的价格向他们提供这些代币。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also support their ability to build agents on top of this.
zh: 我们还支持他们在此基础上构建智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We host what we call sale boxes, which are long-running agent virtual machines hosted in the cloud that are designed for agents that run for hours, days, or weeks.
zh: 我们托管我们所谓的 sale boxes,即托管在云端的长期运行的智能体虚拟机,专为运行数小时、数天或数周的智能体而设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I should think about you as a peer company to others that serve different kinds of inference.
zh: 所以我应该把你视为与其他提供不同类型推理服务的公司对等的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're serving one specific kind of inference, and your goal is to be the absolute cheapest provider and enabler of a certain kind of use of intelligence.
zh: 你提供的是一种特定类型的推理,你的目标是成为某种特定智能使用方式的绝对最便宜的提供者和赋能者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: The theme of our company is abundance.
zh: 我们公司的主题是丰裕。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to deliver this new commodity of intelligence to as many people as possible at a cost that is sustainable for almost every industry.
zh: 我们希望以对几乎每个行业都可持续的成本,把智能这种新商品交付给尽可能多的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think that whenever you make something 10 times cheaper, it's a new product category.
zh: 我们认为,每当你把某样东西变得便宜 10 倍,它就是一个新的产品类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: We aspire to do that for tokens.
zh: 我们立志为代币做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it's so profound that the machine can think, and now our job is to make as many machines as possible in the world.
zh: 我们认为机器能够思考这件事意义如此深远,而现在我们的工作是让世界上尽可能多的机器

speaker: Unknown
en: Work towards thinking.
zh: 向着思考努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about the theme of the day being token costs, is token costs the right way to think about this?
zh: 那么,如果说今天的主题是代币成本,代币成本是思考这件事的正确方式吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there some other way you'd put it?
zh: 你有没有其他表述方式?

speaker: Unknown
en: To start with, absolutely, token costs.
zh: 首先是,绝对是,token 成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my North Stars, I want to have the lowest cost per token in the industry and do that by a mile.
zh: 今天,我的北极星,是做到行业中每 token 成本最低,而且要遥遥领先。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think tokens are the final unit of work or intelligence, but they are what we use today.
zh: 我不认为 token 是最终的工作或智能单位,但它们是我们今天使用的单位。

speaker: Unknown
en: After tokens, you start to move more towards more outcomes, which is like a vague direction.
zh: 在 token 之后,你会开始更偏向于结果,这就像一个模糊的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can imagine, for example, today when you can zoom tokens through an agent, you don't actually control how many tokens the agent reasons for.
zh: 你可以想象,比如,今天当你通过智能体快速消耗 token 时,你实际上并不能控制智能体推理消耗多少 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can reason for a certain amount of time or it can call a certain number of tools.
zh: 它可以推理一段时间,或者调用一定数量的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And increasingly, I think we will have agents do some unit of work, take as many shots on goal as they can.
zh: 而且,我认为我们会越来越多地让智能体完成某个工作单元,尽可能多地进行射门尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And however many tokens they use to get there is going to be a dependent variable depending on the task.
zh: 而它们为此用掉多少 token,将是一个取决于任务的因变量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you think about like agents that self-administer a token budget as opposed to a company setting a budget for how many tokens engineers can spend per month.
zh: 所以你可以想像是智能体自己管理 token 预算,而不是由公司设定工程师每月能花多少 token 的预算。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is there an opportunity that you can tackle?
zh: 为什么存在一个你可以切入的机会?

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like the entire world is oriented around more, better, faster, cheaper tokens right now.
zh: 现在似乎整个世界都在围绕更多、更好、更快的廉价 token 运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like the world is trying to solve this problem very aggressively.
zh: 似乎整个世界都在非常激进地试图解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the unique opening that you saw that's maybe the markets not being efficient in its attempt to tackle this?
zh: 你看到的独特切入点是什么,也许是市场在解决这个问题时不够高效?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's two things that are tailwinds for our company.
zh: 我认为有两件事是我们公司的顺风。

speaker: Unknown
en: One has got to be the rise of open source.
zh: 第一肯定是开源的兴起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had to talk about that first.
zh: 我必须先谈这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're starting to see an increasing number of our customers and the broader market care about owning intelligence.
zh: 我认为我们看到越来越多的客户和更广泛的市场开始在意拥有智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to have control, sovereignty over the thing that they depend on.
zh: 他们想要对所依赖的东西拥有控制权、主权。

speaker: Unknown
en: That created a much more robust market for our customized models or even just like these vanilla open source models that
zh: 这为我们的定制模型,甚至只是这些原生的开源模型,创造了一个健壮得多的市场,

speaker: Unknown
en: No one can ever take away from you.
zh: 没有人能把它从你手里夺走。

speaker: Unknown
en: You always have the weights.
zh: 你永远拥有权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: You always have the right to deploy them however you like.
zh: 你永远有权以你喜欢的方式部署它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that world, there's been a reasonably robust market for the past couple of years serving these models at large scale.
zh: 在那个世界里,过去几年一直有一个相当健壮的市场在大规模服务这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: The challenge is all those companies, you could take your pick, Base 10, Fireworks together, they all focus on low latency inference.
zh: 挑战在于所有那些公司,你可以随便挑,Base 10、Fireworks together,它们全都专注于低延迟推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were pulled in that direction by one very important customer.
zh: 而它们是被一个非常重要的客户拉向那个方向的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cursor.
zh: Cursor。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that that was the right choice about a year ago.
zh: 我认为在一年前那是个正确的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as of six months ago, it started to look like maybe low latency wasn't the only thing you wanted from an agent.
zh: 而到了六个月前,开始显得低延迟也许并不是你对智能体的唯一要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wanted more persistence, more long horizon tasks.
zh: 你想要更多的持续性,更多的长时程任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's to me very obvious that the future of agentic inference is long horizon tasks.
zh: 而现在对我来说非常明显,智能体推理的未来就是长时程任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to run the machine for hours or days at a time.
zh: 你要让机器一次运行几个小时甚至几天。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter if it's been set tokens at 100 tokens per second.
zh: 就算它被设定为每秒 100 个 token 也没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe 10 is just fine if that comes with
zh: 也许每秒 10 个就完全没问题,只要那伴随着

speaker: Unknown
en: Corresponding advantages and efficiency.
zh: 相应的效率和优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you so confident in that?
zh: 你为什么对此如此有信心?

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, it seems like I want everything as fast as possible.
zh: 对我来说,我似乎想要一切都尽可能快。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're waiting on it, you absolutely deserve the fastest answer possible.
zh: 当你在等待结果的时候,你绝对理应得到尽可能快的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: My trick is I don't want you to be waiting on it.
zh: 我的诀窍是,我不想让你在等待它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want it to be proactive.
zh: 我希望它是主动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want it to be in the background.
zh: 我希望它在后台运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: One way to say it is like the best latency is no latency at all.
zh: 一种说法是,最好的延迟就是完全没有延迟。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you wake up in the morning, the work's already been done overnight.
zh: 当你早上醒来,工作已经在夜间完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You didn't even have to ask for it.
zh: 你甚至不需要去请求它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the dream.
zh: 那就是梦想。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not quite there yet.
zh: 我们还没完全到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: More importantly, I think
zh: 更重要的是,我认为

speaker: Unknown
en: The more you're in the loop as you prompt agents and wait for a response.
zh: 当你提示智能体并等待回应时,你越多地处在流程中,

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, you're the bottleneck in having the agent do more or less work.
zh: 事实上,你就是智能体做多或做少工作的瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we'd like is the agent to operate on more human time skills.
zh: 我们想要的是智能体以更多人类时间尺度运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't manage your colleagues every five minutes.
zh: 你不会每五分钟管理一次你的同事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You ask them to do a high-level task and you come back and check in maybe every day, but more likely once a week.
zh: 你让他们做一个高层次的任务，然后回来检查，也许每天一次，但更可能是每周一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that, to me, is the future of human-agent collaboration, more like human time skills.
zh: 对我来说，这就是人机协作的未来，更像人类时间尺度的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say more about the early indications that this is happening and therefore you should be building this company.
zh: 再多说说这种情况正在发生的早期迹象，以及因此你应该创办这家公司的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first and most important thing is the idea of test time compute scaling.
zh: 首先，最重要的事情是测试时计算扩展的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea that you can give an agent more time and it will give you a better answer.
zh: 也就是你可以给智能体更多时间，它就会给你一个更好的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was theorized about two years ago now, but it wasn't really something that we could actually bet on until I would say late last year with Opus 4.5.
zh: 这个想法在大约两年前就被理论化了，但直到我要说是去年年底随着 Opus 4.5 的出现，它才真正成为我们可以押注的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Opus 4.5 was the first agent that was at all suitable for longer horizon tasks.
zh: Opus 4.5 是第一个多少适合更长时间范围任务的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was pretty mediocre when it first came out, but you look at the more recent models and what we've done on open source as well, and you see that agents are capable of running for an hour at a time.
zh: 它刚出来的时候相当平庸，但你看看更新的模型，以及我们在开源方面所做的工作，你会看到智能体能够一次运行一个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't say it's days, but definitely an hour is quite suitable today.
zh: 我不会说是几天，但今天一个小时肯定相当合适。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seeing that like average task length get longer and longer, it doesn't take many points to have you draw out the exponential and see that agents are worth running for longer periods.
zh: 看到平均任务长度越来越长，不需要多少点就能让你画出那条指数曲线，看出智能体值得运行更长的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think will be the market share of long-running agents in three years or something like this?
zh: 你认为长时运行智能体在三年后的市场份额会是多少，诸如此类的问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this market because it's unbounded.
zh: 我喜欢这个市场，因为它是无界的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no human in the loop, so you can consume as many tokens as you like in the background.
zh: 没有人在循环中，所以你可以在后台消耗任意多的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: Versus human attention span, if you tell me to consume 10x as many tokens at Codex or at Claude Code, I'm actually not sure if I can anymore.
zh: 相比之下是人类注意力跨度，如果你让我在 Codex 或 Claude Code 上消耗 10 倍的 token，我其实不确定我还能不能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm already in the loop and locked in coding for most of the day that I'm at the laptop.
zh: 我在笔记本电脑前的大部分时间里已经在循环中、全神贯注地写代码了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is unbounded is how many...
zh: 无界的是多少……

speaker: Unknown
en: Tokens can be consumed in the background or proactively.
zh: token 可以在后台或主动地被消耗。

speaker: Unknown
en: Long-term, I think, you know, we're going to end this year at maybe 50-50 background and real-time workloads, but I see this going to 90-10 in favor of background.
zh: 长期来看，你知道，我认为我们今年会以大概 50 对 50 的后台和实时工作负载结束，但我看到这会走向 90 对 10，偏向后台。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are your favorite examples of something that gets accomplished much better as a background task than as a human in the loop task?
zh: 你最喜欢的哪些例子，作为后台任务比作为人在循环中的任务完成得好得多？

speaker: Unknown
en: Most deep research.
zh: 大多数深度研究。

en: It is so ingrained in every engineer's mind that if the machine can do it, we're going to push the machine to the frontier until it does what we think is.
zh: 这已经深深植根于每位工程师的脑海中:如果机器能做到,我们就会把机器推向前沿,直到它做到我们认为是的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the speed of light is the edge of what's possible.
zh: 光速就是可能性的边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: The speed of light is the edge of what's possible, exactly.
zh: 光速就是可能性的边界,没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we think the chip can run at this frequency and produce this many multiplies per cycle, we're gonna get there.
zh: 如果我们认为芯片能以这个频率运行、每周期执行这么多乘法,我们就要达到那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're gonna break every bottleneck and get to that peak level of performance.
zh: 我们要打破每一个瓶颈,达到那个峰值性能水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: To this day, I tell all my engineers, we're chasing 100% speed of light.
zh: 直到今天,我告诉我所有的工程师,我们追求的是 100% 光速。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care about relative numbers versus the competition.
zh: 我不在乎相对于竞争对手的相对数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: I only care about absolute numbers.
zh: 我只在乎绝对数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are we able to do on the chip?
zh: 我们在这块芯片上能做到什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we achieve that?
zh: 我们如何实现它?

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we leave that chapter of your time at NVIDIA, anything else beyond that cultural touchpoint that changed the way you think about things or that stood out the most about how the business ran back then or its culture?
zh: 在结束你在 NVIDIA 的这段经历之前,除了那个文化触点,还有其他改变你思维方式的东西吗?或者关于当时业务的运作方式或其文化,最让你印象深刻的是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a ton of stories about NVIDIA.
zh: 我有大量关于 NVIDIA 的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could tell you a few of them.
zh: 我可以给你讲几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my favorites is that on the tenure side, a lot of people I worked with in NVIDIA in 2015, 2016 are still there today.
zh: 我最喜欢的之一是关于在职年限的,2015、2016 年和我一起共事的很多人今天还在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That company has incredible retention and these are the best engineers, on the silicon side at least, I've worked with them my whole career.
zh: 那家公司的留任率令人难以置信,而这些是最优秀的工程师,至少在硅片方面,我和他们合作了我的整个职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're extremely, extremely motivated and passionate.
zh: 他们极其、极其有干劲,充满热情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They believed in parallel computing as a concept through its various incarnations and have loved seeing the chip evolve.
zh: 他们经历了并行计算概念的种种形态,始终相信它,并且乐于见证芯片的演进。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is their life's work and they're extremely competent in that direction.
zh: 这是他们毕生的事业,他们在这个方向上极其称职。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're also a very frugal company.
zh: 他们也是一家非常节俭的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA and all the Silicon Valley companies, after 2008, they had some cutbacks and perks.
zh: NVIDIA 和所有硅谷公司,在 2008 年之后,都有过一些削减和取消福利。

speaker: Unknown
en: So no free lunch, for example.
zh: 比如没有免费午餐了。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA took it one step further.
zh: NVIDIA 更进一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no free milk in the fridge.
zh: 冰箱里没有免费牛奶。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you wanted to drink coffee at NVIDIA and you wanted some milk, you'd actually have to chip in a dollar every month to the milk club, and the milk club would stock Costco milk in the fridge.
zh: 所以如果你想在 NVIDIA 喝咖啡,而且想要加点牛奶,你实际上每个月要给牛奶俱乐部凑一块钱,牛奶俱乐部会去 Costco 买牛奶放进冰箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember that distinctly.
zh: 我对这件事记得非常清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't do that at sale.
zh: 我们在 sale 不这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a frugality that permeates.
zh: 这是一种渗透到骨子里的节俭。

speaker: Unknown
en: So coming out of this time there, you get this experience of what it's like to develop more efficient usage of the underlying hardware through software.
zh: 所以从这段经历走出来,你会获得一种体验,那就是通过软件更高效地利用底层硬件是什么感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So link that to today's environment.
zh: 把这个联系到今天的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: The GPU is fundamentally a throughput machine.
zh: GPU 从根本上说是一台吞吐量机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: The GPU is happiest when you give it a lot of work to do and let it chew through that work at peak utilization of its compute units.
zh: 当你给它大量工作去做,并让它以计算单元的峰值利用率消化这些工作时,GPU 是最开心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's actually not the way that we've...
zh: 但这实际上不是我们一直在……

speaker: Unknown
en: Take an AI in the last couple of years.
zh: 拿过去几年的 AI 来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've pushed AI to be an interactive chatbot tool is the most common form of AI usage today.
zh: 我们把 AI 推成了交互式聊天机器人工具,这是当今最常见的 AI 使用形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that world, you care a lot about actually spitting answers out to the person at the keyboard as quickly as possible to your point about don't make the user wait.
zh: 在那个世界里,你非常在意的是尽快把答案吐给键盘前的人,就像你说的,别让用户等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want things as fast as possible.
zh: 我想要东西越快越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually quite interesting for the GPU.
zh: 这对 GPU 来说其实很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very difficult to put the GPU in its happy path of being fully compute utilized when you're trying to spit out tokens quickly.
zh: 当你试图快速吐出 token 时,很难让 GPU 处于计算利用率拉满的理想状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a fundamental tradeoff on the GPU between being throughput oriented or latency optimized.
zh: 在 GPU 上,面向吞吐量和面向延迟优化之间存在着根本性的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone has chosen latency optimization because the shape of usage was chatbot oriented.
zh: 而所有人都选择了延迟优化,因为使用形态是围绕聊天机器人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe that's the most profound change we're going to see in the next year.
zh: 我认为这是未来一年我们将看到的最深刻的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to move away from chatbots to more proactive or background agents.
zh: 我们将从聊天机器人转向更主动的或后台的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: In that world, it makes a lot more sense to build a stack around throughput.
zh: 在那个世界里,围绕吞吐量来构建技术栈就合理得多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you explain technically why the tradeoff between throughput and latency is unbreakable?
zh: 你能从技术上解释一下为什么吞吐量和延迟之间的权衡是不可打破的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't we have both from the same hardware?
zh: 为什么我们不能在同一块硬件上两者兼得?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's quite foundational in almost every system that you could ever possibly look at.
zh: 这在几乎每一个你能看到的系统里都是相当根本性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always a tradeoff between getting a small amount of data through the system as quickly as possible and leaving a lot of buffer room for that or trying to run wide and slow.
zh: 总是在「让少量数据尽可能快地通过系统并为此留出大量缓冲空间」和「试图跑得宽而慢」之间存在权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: Narrow and fast or wide and slow is like a classic tradeoff.
zh: 窄而快还是宽而慢,是一个经典的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: In all computer science.
zh: 在整个计算机科学里都是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for GPU specifically, I think there's one thing to focus on, which is there's this concept of like batching on the GPU.
zh: 但具体到 GPU,我认为有一点值得关注,那就是 GPU 上有个类似批处理的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to group many users' work together into a batch that we can run all at once on the GPU.
zh: 我们想把很多用户的工作归组到一个批次里,以便在 GPU 上一次性全部运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the parallel processing of the GPU.
zh: 这就是 GPU 的并行处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd like to have a lot of parallel work to do.
zh: 我们希望有大量的并行工作可做。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing is, though, you're doing net more work when you run a large batch of compute together.
zh: 但问题在于,当你把一大批计算一起运行时,你净做了更多的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you might be filling all the units, but...
zh: 所以你可能填满了所有单元,但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Every step along the way as you carry a batch of work through the GPU, there's more work to be done.
zh: 当你带着一批工作穿过 GPU 时,沿途每一步都有更多的工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any individual token or any individual user's request in that batch, it's going to spend a longer time on the GPU being carried with other people's traffic.
zh: 批次中的任何一个 token 或任何一个用户的请求,都会在 GPU 上花费更长的时间,与其他人的流量一起被携带。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe the way to say it is if you want to get downtown in SF, you can take the bus or you can take a private transit.
zh: 也许可以这么说,如果你想在 SF 去市中心,你可以坐公交,也可以坐私人交通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the private transit is going to have its own direct path as the crow flies or using exactly the roads that you want from point A to point B.
zh: 私人交通会有自己直达的路径,像乌鸦飞那样直线,或者完全按你想要的从 A 点到 B 点的道路。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to have to serve many more people and it has to fundamentally do something that works for everyone.
zh: 它将不得不服务更多的人,而且它从根本上必须做一些对每个人都行之有效的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it takes a slower path and it stops and waits for other people to get on and off.
zh: 所以它走一条更慢的路线,而且要停下来等人上下车。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the bus versus car analogy is pretty accurate.
zh: 我觉得公交车对小车的类比是相当准确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great analogy and step one for what you're trying to do is create the best possible bus on top of NVIDIA GPUs.
zh: 这个类比很棒,而你们要做的第一步,就是在 NVIDIA GPU 之上打造尽可能好的公交车。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's step one of your optimization.
zh: 就像那是你们优化的第一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means we explore things like different parallelism schemes.
zh: 这意味着我们探索诸如不同的并行方案之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe that's another example I can give you is with NVIDIA GPUs, one of the things that they've really innovated on and done a great job with is the NVLink interconnect between GPUs.
zh: 也许那是我可以给你的另一个例子,关于 NVIDIA GPU,他们真正创新并做得非常出色的其中一件事,就是 GPU 之间的 NVLink 互连。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, that NVLink system is so good that if you have a large matrix multiply that you want to perform faster, you can actually cut that matrix multiply in half and shard it across two or more, up to eight, let's say, NVIDIA GPUs and have them all work on pieces of that larger matrix multiply and have them connect to their results together at the end, reduce their results back together at the end.
zh: 事实上，NVLink 系统好到如果你有一个想更快完成的大型矩阵乘法，你可以把那个矩阵乘法切成两半，分片到两块或更多——比方说最多八块 NVIDIA GPU 上，让它们各自处理那个更大矩阵乘法的一部分，最后再把它们的结果连接起来，在最后把结果归约到一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a great, great way to cut the minimum latency of an operation.
zh: 抱歉——[[310]] 如果你想要尽可能低的最小延迟，你可以这么做，但这不是我我会做的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each GPU is now doing one-eighth as much work, let's say, and therefore it can finish faster, but not eight times faster.
zh: 每块 GPU 现在只做八分之一的工作，比方说，因此它能更快完成，但不会快八倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's sublinear scaling.
zh: 这是亚线性的扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll use eight times more hardware, but you won't get eight times the speed.
zh: 你会用上八倍的硬件，但你不会得到八倍的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might get like four to five X the speed.
zh: 你可能得到大概四到五倍的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to get strong scaling.
zh: 你不会得到强扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is because of communication overhead.
zh: 这是因为通信开销。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's because every GPU is going to be a little less efficient working on a smaller tile of work than a larger tile of work.
zh: 这是因为每块 GPU 在处理较小的任务块时效率都会比处理较大的任务块低一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the only way to speed up.
zh: 这是唯一的提速方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want the minimum latency possible, you can do that, but it is not the choice I would make.
zh: 如果你想要尽可能低的延迟,你可以那么做,但这不是我会做的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, I would prefer to use a different parallelism scheme like expert parallelism or pipeline parallelism.
zh: 例如，我更愿意使用别的并行方案，比如专家并行或流水线并行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We may do interesting things to overlap and hide the communication latency in a way that you would have less.
zh: 我们可能会做一些有意思的事情来重叠和隐藏通信延迟，让你拥有的延迟更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ability to do that for a low latency service.
zh: 对于低延迟服务，做这件事的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So is there a way to think about NVLink as a technology which improves latency performance?
zh: 那么，有没有一种方式可以把 NVLink 看作一项能提升延迟性能的技术？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And only latency performance?
zh: 而且只提升延迟性能？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which will segue into the next segment of what we do differently as a company.
zh: 这会引出我们作为一家公司做了哪些不同事情的下一个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yes, NVLink is mandatory for low latency inference.
zh: 但是的，NVLink 对于低延迟推理是必需的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So NVIDIA is excellent at low latency inference.
zh: 所以 NVIDIA 非常擅长低延迟推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm telling you that we don't really care that much about low latency inference.
zh: 而我告诉你，我们并不那么在意低延迟推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So where does that leave us?
zh: 那么这对我们意味着什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not holding my breath for other companies, broadly, to figure out NVLink quickly.
zh: 我不会指望其他公司总体上能很快搞懂 NVLink。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a challenging technology to figure out.
zh: 这是一项很难搞懂的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to scale.
zh: 它很难扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to productionize.
zh: 它很难产品化。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I do have some other vendor's chip and it is good at the foundational compute components, it can still do which multiplies really well.
zh: 如果我手上确实有其他厂商的芯片，而且它擅长基础计算部件，它仍然可以把矩阵乘法做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just can't communicate those results across its peers quickly.
zh: 它只是无法快速把这些结果在同级芯片之间传递。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, maybe there's room for that other chip in my stack as a
zh: 那么，也许那块其他芯片在我的技术栈里仍有一席之地，作为一种

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, really good compute per dollar option.
zh: 非常、非常好的每美元算力选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I actually optimize for in most cases is how many flops does this chip have and how much is it going to cost me per hour to own and operate.
zh: 在大多数情况下，我真正优化的是这块芯片有多少 flops，以及拥有和运行它每小时要花我多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are other chips that definitely rank higher than NVIDIA on flops per dollar but they may not have as much interconnect.
zh: 确实有一些芯片在每美元 flops 上排名高于 NVIDIA，但它们可能没有那么多互联。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's my job to figure out what parallelism scheme am I going to use that's going to make this chip suitable for inference.
zh: 所以我的工作就是想清楚我要用什么样的并行方案，才能让这块芯片适合推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not going to be tensor parallelism.
zh: 那不会是张量并行。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is basically mandatory for that.
zh: NVIDIA 对那来说基本是必需的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But other techniques may work well for me.
zh: 但其他技术可能对我很有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before we leave the latency part of the story, can you comment on companies like Cerebris or others that can perform incredibly fast operations?
zh: 那么，在我们离开延迟这部分故事之前，你能谈谈像 Cerebris 或其他那些能执行极快操作的公司吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what you think about those approaches, those companies, what might happen in the future?
zh: 我很好奇你对那些方法、那些公司怎么看，未来可能会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your prediction for the future of very low latency focused hardware?
zh: 你对聚焦超低延迟硬件的未来有什么预测？

speaker: Unknown
en: Cerebrus, Grok, and a couple others that are coming out of stealth now, I think have made a very interesting bet on not just building another GPU, but actually building a different kind of accelerator that focuses on a different memory hierarchy.
zh: Cerebrus、Grok，还有几家现在正走出隐身模式的公司，我认为他们下了一个非常有意思的赌注：不只是再造一块 GPU，而是真正造一种不同类型的加速器，聚焦于不同的内存层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want to maximize the amount of SRAM on the chip and use that as very, very fast memory for weights and KV cache.
zh: 他们想最大化芯片上的 SRAM 数量，并把它用作非常非常快的内存来存放权重和 KV cache。

speaker: Unknown
en: So SRAM versus DRAM, there's two ways to make memory for a chip.
zh: SRAM 与 DRAM 相比，为芯片制造内存有两种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is to integrate the memory on the logic die itself, meaning you tell TSMC, I want this many megabytes of storage on my chip, and there's a way to build that.
zh: 一种是把内存集成在逻辑裸片本身上，意思是你告诉 TSMC，我要在我的芯片上放这么多兆字节的存储，而这是有办法造出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: TSMC has a standard cell library you can use, and you can just print out a bunch of cells of SRAM.
zh: TSMC 有一个你可以使用的标准单元库，你可以直接印出一堆 SRAM 单元。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem with SRAM is it takes a lot of area on the silicon die.
zh: SRAM 的问题在于它会占用硅裸片上大量的面积。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you want to build a large die, like let's say the NVIDIA Blackwell at 800 millimeters square, if you made that whole die SRAM, it would be in the maybe like single digit gigabytes, it feels like.
zh: 所以如果你想造一个大裸片，比方说 800 平方毫米的 NVIDIA Blackwell，如果你把整个裸片都做成 SRAM，感觉大概是几个 GB 量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not a crazy amount of data storage.
zh: 这不算一个疯狂的存储量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compare that to if you're willing to take a different process technology entirely, so not TSMC anymore, but now Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung.
zh: 对比一下，如果你愿意采用一种完全不同的工艺技术，就不再是 TSMC 了，而是 Micron、SK Hynix、三星。

speaker: Unknown
en: They build DRAM, which is a whole different way to build memory that's more focused on capacitors than transistor cells.
zh: 他们造 DRAM，那是一种完全不同的造内存的方式，更聚焦于电容而不是晶体管单元。

speaker: Unknown
en: The standard way to build SRAM is what's called the 6T transistor cell.
zh: 造 SRAM 的标准方式是所谓的 6T 晶体管单元。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a stable transistor arrangement that allows you to write a bit to it and then it holds that state in that bit, regardless of whether you keep applying, well, you had to apply some power, but it's holding that bit without any sort of like active management.
zh: 它是一种稳定的晶体管排列方式，允许你向其中写入一个位，然后它就会保持那个位的状态，不管你是否持续施加——嗯，你得施加一些电力——但它是在没有任何主动管理的情况下保持那个位。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's static.
zh: 它是静态的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, dynamic RAM, DRAM, it's dynamic because what you do to write some data is you write a charge onto a capacitor, and as soon as you write that charge into that capacitor, the charge is dissipating.
zh: 现在，动态 RAM,DRAM,它之所以是动态的，是因为你写数据的方式是把一个电荷写到一个电容上，而一旦你把那个电荷写进那个电容，电荷就在耗散。

speaker: Unknown
en: The dynamic part of DRAM is that you must, every 50 milliseconds or so, refresh every bit you've written.

en: 10 megawatts is probably on the edge of what's possible today.

en: And one megawatt, I would argue, is plentiful.

en: I think if you look at the entropy in a KVCache, it's not earning its keep.
zh: 我觉得如果你看 KVCache 里的熵，它并不值这个存储成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're storing many kilobytes of data in the KVCache per token.
zh: 比如说，我们每个 token 在 KVCache 里存储了好几千字节的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's probably off by an order of magnitude or two.
zh: 而这很可能差了一到两个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know the frontier labs do, but DeepSeq certainly publishes really interesting work to compress that further and further.
zh: 我不知道前沿实验室的情况，但 DeepSeq 肯定发布了非常有趣的工作来把这个进一步压缩再压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're making good progress.
zh: 而且他们正在取得很好的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the fact that they're able to make an order of magnitude and progress here every year or so signals that there's a lot more room to go.
zh: 我认为，他们大约每年就能在这个方向上取得一个数量级的进展，这本身就表明还有很大的提升空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you zoom out further, I think that we actually don't marshal our compute effectively at all.
zh: 如果再往宏观层面看，我认为我们实际上完全没有有效地调度我们的算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have all this compute in the world.
zh: 世界上有这么多算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is pumping out 5 million Blackwell chips this year.
zh: NVIDIA 今年正在产出 500 万颗 Blackwell 芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are they all going?
zh: 它们都去哪儿了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they all being used at all all the time?
zh: 它们真的都在被全天候地使用吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I certainly doubt it.
zh: 我肯定对此表示怀疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that at some level we just need better orchestration of compute across the world.
zh: 我认为在某种程度上，我们只需要在全球范围内对算力进行更好的编排。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is very difficult to do because a lot of the compute disappears into private pools of compute that will never suit the light of day and those GPUs sit very sadly idle.
zh: 这非常难做到，因为很多算力都消失在永远不会见天日的私有算力池里，那些 GPU 非常悲哀地闲置着。

speaker: Unknown
en: It pains me physically to see that those GPUs are just silicon and power going into that and it's just sitting idle and I want to fix that.
zh: 看到那些 GPU 只是硅片和电力的投入却闲置在那里，我身体上都感到痛苦，我想修复这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: How we organize and orchestrate the world's compute as a shared resource and pack it more efficiently, I would estimate that
zh: 我们如何组织和编排世界算力作为一个共享资源，并更高效地打包它，我估计

speaker: Unknown
en: We all make fun of xAI for having, you know, some challenges with total flop utilization on its clusters.
zh: 我们都取笑 xAI，你知道的，它的集群在总 flop 利用率上存在一些挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reality for the rest of the world is it's far worse.
zh: 而对世界上其他地方来说，现实要糟糕得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: A ton of GPUs just sit in warehouses or sit in private pools allocated to a specific customer.
zh: 大量的 GPU 就堆在仓库里，或者待在分配给特定客户的私有算力池里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just don't get utilized.
zh: 就是得不到利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're attacking the efficiency of that very directly.
zh: 你正在非常直接地攻那里的效率问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's way more effective, yeah.
zh: 那要有效得多，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about fabs?
zh: 那晶圆厂呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think is the future of fabs themselves?
zh: 你认为晶圆厂本身的未来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everyone is wondering, will the memory companies, will TSMC, will Intel and others, how will they expand capacity basically?
zh: 我想每个人都在好奇，那些内存公司、TSMC、Intel 以及其他公司，它们基本上会如何扩充产能？

speaker: Unknown
en: Will we do it here in the US?
zh: 我们会在美国本土做到这一点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Riff on fabrication of chips themselves.
zh: 随便聊聊芯片制造本身吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if we could just snap our fingers and have a hundred times the chips in the stock today, we'd probably have way cheaper tokens.
zh: 比如如果我们能打个响指就拥有比今天库存多一百倍的芯片，我们的 token 可能会便宜得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That seems like an important part of the universe to hear your view on.
zh: 这似乎是宇宙中很重要的一部分，值得听听你的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything grows in balance with each other.
zh: 万物都是彼此均衡地增长的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we snap our fingers and double all those things, you might fix a TSMC bottleneck, you're just going to run into another bottleneck.
zh: 如果我们打个响指把所有这些东西翻倍，你可能修复了 TSMC 这个瓶颈，但你只会撞上另一个瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: You make 20% more chips, then you have another bottleneck immediately.
zh: 你多生产 20% 的芯片，然后立刻又出现另一个瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will say, though, it is interesting what they consider to be a must-deliver, like an invariant that their customers, me, are always going to want, versus what I think is like a more fluid relationship.
zh: 不过我要说，有意思的是他们认为什么是必须交付的，比如一个他们的客户（也就是我）永远都会想要的不变量，而什么在我看来更像是一种更灵活的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that if the fab exposes more of their trade-offs to me,
zh: 我认为，如果晶圆厂向我暴露更多他们的权衡取舍，

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm able to make more intelligent decisions about what I can do.
zh: 我就能对我能做的事情做出更智能的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most interesting examples here is that Anyfab has a lot of spread in their worst chip that comes out of the production line and the best chip that comes out of the production line.
zh: 这里最有趣的例子之一是，Anyfab 从生产线上出来的最差芯片和最好芯片之间存在很大的离散度。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of variance in how chips are made.
zh: 芯片的制造过程存在很大的方差。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the question is, if you have a company like TSMC, they work very, very hard to tighten what we call these process corners.
zh: 而问题是，如果你有一家像 TSMC 这样的公司，他们会非常非常努力地收紧我们所说的这些工艺角。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to keep the worst chip
zh: 我们想让最差的芯片

speaker: Unknown
en: As close in characterization to the best chip.
zh: 在特性上尽可能接近最好的芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they've got a great lens to make that possible.
zh: 而他们有一个很好的视角来实现这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that means that they are adding a lot of controls in the process that maybe I don't need.
zh: 但这意味着他们在工艺中加入了大量我可能并不需要的控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'm actually willing to find a place for that worst chip.
zh: 也许我实际上愿意为那颗最差的芯片找个位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to tighten the process control as much, which takes more time and cost.
zh: 你不需要把工艺控制收得那么紧，而收紧控制需要更多时间和成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'm willing to take a lot more rejects.
zh: 也许我愿意接受多得多的不良品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think for us it's like a more holistic optimization around cost of the dyes, supply of the dyes, and then the cost of power and places we can put them.
zh: 我认为对我们来说，这是一种围绕裸片成本、裸片供应，以及电力成本和可放置地点的更整体性的优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: My whole goal is to so dramatically expand the supply of power across the United States that I have a home for a lot of ships that otherwise would not have earned their place in a data center.
zh: 我的整个目标是极大地扩展全美国的电力供应，这样我就能为许多原本无法在数据中心赢得一席之地的芯片找到归宿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we talk about
zh: 我们能不能谈谈

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you design the system of your own business?
zh: 你如何设计自己业务的系统？

speaker: Unknown
en: What lessons have you learned?
zh: 你学到了哪些经验教训？

speaker: Unknown
en: You talked about some interesting NVIDIA lessons.
zh: 你提到过一些有趣的 NVIDIA 经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bring me into the culture and how you structure a team and a business where this is the North Star.
zh: 带我了解一下你们的文化，以及你如何构建一个以此为北极星的团队和企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of in the limit thinking.
zh: 我们有很多极限思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't worry about the immediate nature of when we start working on a model, the efficiency is not going to be very good.
zh: 我们不担心开始研究一个模型时的眼前状况，那时的效率不会很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think about like where we could end up in like a month, six months or a year's time.
zh: 我们想的是比如一个月、六个月或一年后我们可能达到的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't accept the state of the machines we work on is fixed.
zh: 我们不接受我们所使用的机器的状态是固定不变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even something like the Blackwell chip, if we think that there's some bottleneck that is holding us back from achieving this performance, it's very important to me that we understand and characterize that very well and write it down so we can both A, tell NVIDIA about it, who are friends, and also to basically keep this in mind for future chips that we buy.
zh: 即使是 Blackwell 芯片这样的东西，如果我们认为存在某个瓶颈阻碍我们达到这个性能，对我来说非常重要的是，我们要很好地理解并刻画它，并把它写下来，这样我们既能 A、告诉 NVIDIA——他们是朋友——也能为将来购买的芯片把这一点记在心里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to learn things that are invariant for us or the company long term.
zh: 我们想学习那些对我们或公司长期而言不变的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of fold that into future decisions that we make.
zh: 并把它融入我们未来所做的决策中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're very collaborative.
zh: 我们非常协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one of the most important traits that we look for are people who are both good students and great teachers.
zh: 我认为我们寻找的最重要的特质之一，是那些既是好学生又是好老师的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of our people on the team were TAs in college and loved the experience of sharing knowledge in this way.
zh: 我们团队里的很多人在大学时当过助教，并且热爱这种分享知识的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do whiteboard sessions all the time.
zh: 我们经常开白板讨论会。

speaker: Unknown
en: The collegial environment where everyone has something to teach and something to learn is extremely important for us.
zh: 人人都有东西可教、有东西可学的这种同事式环境对我们极其重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the attributes of people that you would want to hire that you think will be resilient to the work environment three years from now when more stuff is handled by machines?
zh: 你想雇用的人需要具备哪些特质，你认为他们在三年后、当更多事情由机器处理时，能够适应那样的工作环境？

speaker: Unknown
en: Curiosity.
zh: 好奇心。

speaker: Unknown
en: 100% curiosity.
zh: 百分之百是好奇心。

speaker: Unknown
en: The one thing I cannot teach is love for performance.
zh: 有一件事我无法传授，就是对性能的热爱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love for digging into every microsecond the machine is working and understanding what's happening on the machine at that time.
zh: 热爱深挖机器运行的每一个微秒，理解那一刻机器上正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That, to me, is the most important trait for a performance engineer.
zh: 对我来说，这是性能工程师最重要的特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what I look for.
zh: 这就是我寻找的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't look for lots of AI experience.
zh: 我不寻找大量的 AI 经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't look for CUDA experience at all.
zh: 我完全不寻找 CUDA 经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually a huge red herring.
zh: 那其实是一个巨大的误导。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, CUDA as a concept or GPS as a concept have evolved so much in the last five years.
zh: 我的意思是，CUDA 作为一个概念，或者 GPU 作为一个概念，在过去五年里已经演进得太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no point asking for 10 years of experience.
zh: 要求十年经验毫无意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to teach that, but I cannot teach the love for performance engineering.
zh: 我想去教那些东西，但我无法教对性能工程的热爱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is what I seek.
zh: 那正是我寻求的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you give your assessment of the major labs one by one, but also then the relationship of closed source as a category to open source, what you think is happening and will happen?
zh: 你能否逐一给出对各大实验室的评估，还有闭源作为一个类别与开源的关系——你认为正在发生什么、将会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: In a line, I would say the labs pay an immense premium to be three to six months ahead of everything else.
zh: 一句话概括，我认为这些实验室为领先其他一切三到六个月支付了巨大的溢价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's probably still worth it.
zh: 我认为这可能仍然值得。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it makes perfect sense for it.
zh: 我认为这对它们来说完全合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic to do what they do.
zh: 让 Anthropic 做它们在做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a sensitive topic around distillation, which I think is a very core piece of the relationship between closed and open frontier.
zh: 有一个关于蒸馏的敏感话题，我认为这是闭源与开源前沿之间关系的非常核心的一环。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd like to offer an alternative view on that, which is there is the sense that distillation is theft, that you are taking something from the frontier models when you distill on their outputs.
zh: 我想就此提出一个不同的看法，即有一种观点认为蒸馏就是盗窃，当你对前沿模型的输出做蒸馏时，你是在从它们那里拿走一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, even if that's not your intent, even if you don't ever try to scrape data from Anthropic, one thing I'll offer is that an increasingly large percentage of the artifacts we put out on the internet are AI generated.
zh: 而事实上，即使那不是你的意图，即使你从不试图去抓取 Anthropic 的数据，我要提出的一点是，我们在互联网上发布的产物中，越来越大的百分比是 AI 生成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just look at GitHub alone.
zh: 你只看 GitHub 就知道了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What percentage of repos created in the last year do we think were created by Claude Code?
zh: 我们认为过去一年创建的仓库中有多大比例是由 Claude Code 创建的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we consider that to be distillation?
zh: 我们认为这算蒸馏吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's probably all we need.
zh: 因为它可能就是我们所需的全部。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would not be surprised if you could train a Fable class model only on the outputs of code you consider good on GitHub that's open source.
zh: 如果你只用在 GitHub 上你认为好的开源代码的输出，就能训练出一个 Fable 级别的模型，我不会感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And certainly if we take the position that users own the outputs of their interaction with AI and they choose to put that up on GitHub, which a lot of them do, we're going to have latent distillation for a long time.
zh: 而且当然，如果我们采取这样一个立场：用户拥有他们与 AI 交互产生的输出，并且他们选择把这些放到 GitHub 上——很多人确实这么做——那么隐性蒸馏将会存在很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems fundamentally possible for me.
zh: 对我来说，这看起来在根本上是可以实现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's fundamentally possible to prevent the diffusion of information or model capabilities.
zh: 我不认为在根本上可以阻止信息或模型能力的扩散。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will happen.
zh: 它会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is just how fast.
zh: 问题只是有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then the question becomes, do scaling and improvement laws hold forever or for a really long period of time?
zh: 于是问题就变成，规模化和改进的定律会永远成立，还是会成立很长一段时间？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they do, then there's value to being three to six months ahead and that will just last as long as it lasts and they can charge a huge premium for those tokens relative to a very cheap open source token.
zh: 如果成立，那么领先三到六个月就有价值，而且这种价值会持续存在多久就多久，他们可以对这些 token 收取巨大的溢价，相对于非常便宜的开源 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the right way to think about it?
zh: 这是对这个问题正确的思考方式吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's possible.
zh: 我认为有可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know that the premium for being three to six months ahead is going to last that long.
zh: 我不知道领先三到六个月的溢价会持续那么久。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you look at like enterprise deployments,
zh: 我是说，如果你看看企业级部署，

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't move at three to six months speed.
zh: 它们不是以三到六个月的速度行动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of enterprises are probably still handling 4.6, Opus 4.6 or Opus 4.7.
zh: 很多企业可能还在用 4.6、Opus 4.6 或 Opus 4.7。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't adopt the bleeding edge rapidly.
zh: 它们不会快速采用最前沿的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of questions that people have around rolling out any change at all.
zh: 人们对推行任何改动都有很多疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just so early in scratching the surface that I don't think there's any way to call a winner in this race.
zh: 我们才刚刚触及皮毛，以至于我认为没有任何办法在这场竞赛中判定赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly, I don't even think this is a race that can be decided ever.
zh: 当然，我甚至不认为这是一场能被裁决出来的竞赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a continual process.
zh: 它是一个持续的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, I don't think open source ever goes away.
zh: 根本上，我不认为开源会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there's a vacuum because one leader steps out, a new leader will step in.
zh: 如果因为一个领导者退出而出现真空，新的领导者会补上。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's too much incentive and too much tailwinds too.
zh: 动力太大了，顺风也太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It gets easier every day to train a frontier class model.
zh: 训练一个前沿级别的模型每天都变得更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So your hope of what the future looks like is what balance between closed and open, what balance between model companies doing everything because they have the advantage of owning the stack or whatever.
zh: 那么你对未来的期望是什么样的平衡？封闭和开源之间是什么平衡？模型公司因为拥有整个技术栈的优势而包揽一切，还是别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic can do that.
zh: Anthropic 可以那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the new Google would just do that or something.
zh: → [[997]] 你的哪些想法会让你的朋友们看你的眼神像是你长了三颗头？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you hope the future looks like?
zh: 你希望未来是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: I want abundant tokens and diverse harnesses.
zh: 我想要充裕的 token 和多样的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want everyone to build their own harness.
zh: 我想要每个人都构建自己的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every company, every user, even.
zh: 每家公司，甚至每个用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Make the agent your own.
zh: 让智能体成为你自己的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not that far away from that level of customization and capability.
zh: 我们离那种定制化和能力的水平并不遥远。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want people to own their intelligence, and I want that intelligence to be customized, probably not through weight fine-tuning, but probably through more in-context learning.
zh: 我想要人们拥有自己的智能，我想要那种智能被定制化，可能不是通过权重微调，而是更多地通过上下文学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a more technical detail, but the underlying input to this abundant future is about cheap tokens.
zh: 这是个更技术性的细节，但这个充裕未来的底层输入在于便宜的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: My job is to make the tokens as cheap as humanly possible.
zh: 我的工作就是把 token 做到人类可能做到的最低价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will achieve that and I will do it through every layer in the stack available to me.
zh: 我会实现这一点，而且我会通过技术栈中我可用的每一层来实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the supply side levers.
zh: 我喜欢供给侧的杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will use every chip.
zh: 我会用每一块芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll use every source of power and I will use every piece of land in the United States that's suitable for this.
zh: 我会用每一种电力来源，我会用美国每一块适合做这件事的土地。

speaker: Unknown
en: In return, people will have the incentive to explore what it's like to have abundant intelligence.
zh: 作为回报，人们会有动力去探索拥有充裕智能是什么感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still treat the agent as a person that is expensive to consult and you should ask them when you have a hard question.
